name: Example: Calculating Dot Products Using Orthogonal Vectors
problem: Let ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044739/assets/61cb89adc9a0cce6a434c41be5d2d1799e01e94bebe1b4f44d48bc011c1a349b.png) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044739/assets/00af13e5017635a0b333ecd5fc2bfc761c9612427b8a3986ba48fa904ff2eed0.png) be vectors such that $\mathbf{u} \!\perp\! \mathbf{w}$. Find $(\mathbf{u}+\mathbf{v})\cdot \mathbf{w} + \mathbf{u}\cdot(\mathbf{v}+ \mathbf{w}).$
worked_solution:
Since $\mathbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{w}$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that $\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{w}=0$. Therefore, using linearity of the dot product to expand the parentheses, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(u+v)\cdot w+u\cdot (v+w) & =u\cdot w+v\cdot w+u\cdot v+u\cdot w \\  & =0+v\cdot w+u\cdot v+0 \\  & =v\cdot w+u\cdot v \\  & =(2\cdot (-1)+(-3)\cdot 3+4\cdot 1) \\  & +((-1)\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot (-3)+5\cdot 4)\, \\  & =(-2-9+4)+(-2+6+20) \\  & =-7+24 \\  & =17.\end{aligned}
$$
